P-01-krt-karta.текст: A cinematic ultra-premium editorial cover photograph, 16:9 horizontal, of a large physical planning table shot from a high three-quarter angle in a dark architectural studio, showing a precisely milled scale relief map of Moscow inside the MKAD ring: the map is a real tactile object made of matte graphite-grey machined composite in the exact colour #14171C, with the river channel, the ring road and the radial arteries cut as thin engraved grooves filled with warm white #F5F1E8 lines only one millimetre wide, the whole board resting on a scuffed steel frame with visible weld seams, oxidised bolt heads, chipped edge paint and fine dust in the corners so the object reads as a working instrument that has been used for years and never as a clean stock render. Across the southern and south-eastern part of the board eleven irregular industrial land parcels are physically recessed into the surface and covered with dull dead grey matte panels in #14171C, slightly lower than the rest of the relief, unlit, colour drained, their edges bevelled and dusty, reading unmistakably as switched off and condemned; scattered across those grey zones lie tiny extinguished factory blocks, sheds and stacks, all in the same lifeless graphite. One single parcel, positioned in the lower left third of the board, is different: it stands proud of the surface, machined in the same graphite but crowned by one intense amber #E8A400 point of light set into the material like a fibre-optic marker, throwing a real hot pool of light and a soft warm halo across the neighbouring relief, with a thin concentric amber ring engraved around it and a fine muted gold #C9A233 leader line running out of it to the edge of the board; this amber point is the only saturated colour anywhere in the frame and it is unmistakably outside every grey recessed parcel. The Russian headline is physically part of the scene, deep-engraved and paint-filled into a brushed steel plate that is bolted flat onto the near lower edge of the map board, lying in the same perspective as the table so the letters foreshorten correctly and catch the raking light along their machined bevels: it reads exactly, character by character, in Russian Cyrillic, the string "ЗИЛ СТАЛ ЖИЛЫМ КВАРТАЛОМ" rendered without the quotation marks themselves, set in a dense modern condensed grotesque, all capitals, wide letter tracking, filled with warm white #F5F1E8 paint, occupying roughly seventy percent of the frame width and about eleven percent of the frame height, one single line with no hyphenation, the largest typographic element in the image. Directly beneath it, engraved smaller into the same steel plate, the secondary line reads exactly the string "Проверьте свой адрес за 4 минуты" rendered without the quotation marks themselves, at about forty percent of the frame width and roughly one third the cap height of the headline, in the same grotesque with technical-documentation spacing, where the numeral 4 is rendered noticeably larger and filled with amber #E8A400 so the number is the visual anchor of the sub-line while every other character stays warm white #F5F1E8. Lighting is a single hard directional key from the upper left at a low forty-degree rake, like an architectural photography shoot, sculpting long deep shadows off the raised parcels and the bolt heads, deep falloff into near-black at the top right corner, plus the amber point light acting as the only warm practical source in the scene and the only thing that glows. The entire palette is strictly limited to amber #E8A400, muted gold #C9A233, graphite #14171C, ink black #0E1116 and warm white #F5F1E8; absolutely no other colour is permitted anywhere, including in reflections, spill light, bounce and shadow tint, no blue, no green, no red, no teal, no neon, no cyberpunk glow. Materials must show honest wear: micro-scratches on the steel plate, fingerprint smears, faint dust, slightly worn paint in the engraved grooves, subtle grain, shallow depth of field softening only the far top edge of the board. No people anywhere. Photographic, medium-format look, 40mm equivalent lens, crisp micro-contrast, editorial business-magazine cover quality. Beneath it, painted smaller on the lower band of the same hoarding, the secondary line reads exactly the string "4 минуты и кадастровый номер" rendered without the quotation marks themselves, at about thirty-five percent of the frame width and roughly one quarter the cap height of the headline, in the same grotesque with documentation-style letter spacing, where the numeral 4 is markedly larger and painted in amber #E8A400 so the number reads as the hero digit, while every remaining character stays warm white #F5F1E8. Lighting is late low-angle directional sun from the far left, raking hard across the industrial half so the concrete texture and the corrugation of the hoarding are sculpted by long deep shadows, while the residential half falls into cooler flat shade with deep ink-black #0E1116 window voids; a single amber #E8A400 practical, a work lamp under the loading gate on the left, throws the only warm pool of light in the scene and the only glow, spilling faintly onto the wet concrete and the base of the hoarding. Lighting is a single strong directional key entering through the gate from the upper right at a shallow angle, cutting a hard bright wedge across the polished floor and throwing long deep shadows off the columns and the crane beam back toward the camera, with heavy falloff into ink-black #0E1116 in the ceiling trusses and the side aisles; one amber #E8A400 sodium work lamp mounted high on the left column is the only warm practical in the scene, glowing softly and laying a warm reflected streak on the wet-looking polished concrete, and it is the only light source that glows in the frame. The ground plane is cracked concrete apron with survey stakes, a chalk line, a chain-link section leaning, and shallow puddles that mirror the crane silhouette in broken warm-white reflections.
